stories.title: OpenAI withdraws 3 math papers after mathematicians call its proofs substandard
stories.summary: OpenAI retracted three AI-generated math papers after a sign error was found, and mathematicians are calling for a boycott after the company released over 700 proofs at once, saying they deviate from field standards.
stories.more: The Association for Human Mathematics called for an OpenAI boycott after the company flooded the field with more than 700 AI-generated math manuscripts in one batch. OpenAI had to retract three of those papers the next day over a sign error. TechCrunch reports the proofs deviated from guidelines set by mathematical researchers OpenAI had consulted. Fields Medalist Terence Tao warned that this kind of mass "harvesting" of open problems could leave entire branches of mathematics less fertile for future work. The withdrawal was also discussed heavily on Hacker News, where two separate threads covered the retraction.

The debate reflects growing unease in the crypto community about AI's mathematical capabilities outpacing cryptographic assumptions.

stories.title: STEPQuant paper tackles quantization errors in linear-attention recurrent states
stories.summary: A new paper introduces STEPQuant, studying how quantization errors in delta-rule linear-attention models' recurrent states vary by when and where they occur, aiming to cut memory use without hurting accuracy.
stories.more: Linear attention models replace growing KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states, but these states become a memory bottleneck during concurrent serving. Directly quantizing them to low precision has previously caused accuracy to degrade because errors compound across decoding steps. The authors find that error impact depends on two dimensions: how long an error persists in memory, and the state's structural position. STEPQuant proposes a quantization approach informed by these findings. Benchmark results are not disclosed in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Long-WAM paper scales context length for real-time robot world-action models
stories.summary: Researchers present Long-WAM, a framework for giving world-action models in robot control much longer visual history while still meeting real-time constraints.
stories.more: Real-time robot control needs enough visual history to track motion and task progress, but processing long histories can introduce delay. The paper's central finding is that simply having access to history isn't the same as using it effectively: longer histories help most when the underlying video model was pretrained autoregressively. The authors first train causal prediction on robot and egocentric video before scaling context. Benchmark numbers are not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: GRACE paper proposes generation-aware latent compression for video diffusion
stories.summary: A new paper, GRACE, targets the trade-off between compression and quality in video autoencoders used by diffusion transformers, aiming to speed up video generation without costly retraining.
stories.more: Highly compressed video autoencoders can speed up video diffusion models since the diffusion transformer processes fewer tokens, but higher compression typically hurts reconstruction quality and needs more channels, slowing convergence. Because a new compressed latent differs from what a pretrained diffusion transformer was trained on, that model usually must be retrained or adapted. GRACE is framed as a generation-aware approach to this compression problem. The excerpt does not specify exact compression ratios or quality results achieved.

stories.title: VepAgent uses tool-augmented reinforcement learning for video event prediction
stories.summary: Researchers introduce VepAgent, an agentic framework combining causal-transition reasoning with reinforcement learning to help multimodal models predict future events in video.
stories.more: Multimodal large language models have shown promise on video understanding but tend to rely on retrospective summarization and text-centric priors, limiting their ability to reason about unobserved causal transitions for video event prediction. VepAgent instead integrates causal-transition reasoning with tool-augmented reinforcement learning. The paper contrasts this with prior methods that passively project forward rather than actively reasoning about causality. Specific performance gains are not given in the available excerpt.

stories.title: UniWAM unifies world modeling and action prediction for robots
stories.summary: A new architecture, UniWAM, combines a physical reasoner, a world generator, and an action predictor to address weaknesses in both vision-language-action and world-action models.
stories.more: Vision-language-action models benefit from pretrained vision-language understanding but have limited grounding in physical world dynamics since they rely only on action supervision. World-action models, conversely, inherit useful spatiotemporal priors from video generation but are weaker at semantic reasoning under distribution shift. UniWAM aims to unify these strengths in one architecture with three components: a physical reasoner, a world generator, and an action predictor. The excerpt does not include evaluation results.

stories.title: Tetris3D generates 3D scenes with objects that fit together geometrically
stories.summary: A new generative framework, Tetris3D, reconstructs 3D scenes from a single image so that objects are physically and geometrically coherent with their neighbors, rather than placed independently.
stories.more: Existing single-image 3D scene reconstruction methods often generate objects independently or only implicitly couple them, giving limited guidance for spatial compatibility between neighboring objects. Tetris3D explicitly conditions each object's generation on the geometry of surrounding objects. The goal is scenes where objects fit together the way they would in reality. The excerpt does not report quantitative results.
